_comment: The potion belt's four slots, the ones bound to keys 1-4.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS: the keys used to be written out by hand in user_config.txt, which
meant the program pressed '2' for a rejuvenation potion whether or not one was there.
Rearrange the belt and it drinks the wrong thing; empty a column and it presses a dead
key while dying. The slots are on screen, so they can be read instead of declared.
ONLY THE BOTTOM ROW MATTERS and the belt does not need to be open. Diablo II shows that
row on the HUD at all times, and it is the row bound to 1-4; the other three rows of a
full belt are reserves that feed it. Confirmed against the owner's opened-belt screenshot.
MEASURED on four real frames (three potion types plus an empty slot), at the insets
below - an occupied slot is 26-37% lit and an empty one is 0.0%, with modal hues 0 for
red healing, 118 for blue mana and 151 for purple rejuvenation. The gaps are enormous
because these are different colours of the same glass, which is exactly the job an HSV
mask is for and exactly the job template matching cannot do (TM_CCOEFF_NORMED is very
region and the keys are fractions of / bound to the ANCHOR WINDOW, so this survives the
game being windowed, moved or resized. Recalibrate if the game's resolution changes: the
HUD re-lays out, exactly as meters.json does.
Red wraps the end of the hue circle, so healing needs two ranges. Same reason meters.json
